feedback: Approving this candidate so it races. It has not raced, so I state no outcome for it. The design is valid: all values are inside the contract ranges, and the sensor layout, base_speed 1.3, ki 0 and line_loss 'last_direction' match the best raced design (iteration 1, score 556.7). The only changes are kp 3.5 to 3.8 and kd 0.6 to 0.7. Iteration 1 showed that a stronger correction (kp 2.5 to 3.5, with kd 0.3 to 0.6) raised the score from 317.4 to 556.7, with the oval finishing 20/20. Iteration 2 showed that cutting speed to 1.2 lowered the score to 521.7, so speed is not the lever to pull now. The main risk is that kp 3.8 raises steering oscillation, which was already 0.37 on the s-bend in iteration 1, and that it pushes the oval off track. Once the race reports back, compare per-track completion, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation against iterations 1 and 2 before choosing the next step. If the oval still finishes and steering_oscillation stays near or below 0.37, keep kp 3.8 and test whether kd 0.8 or line_loss 'search_left'/'search_right' helps the slalom. If the oval shows off-track exits or steering_oscillation rises well above 0.37, step back to kp 3.5 with kd 0.8 rather than raising kp again.
requested_changes: After the race: if the oval still finishes 20/20 and steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.37, keep kp 3.8 and try kd 0.8 to damp the stronger correction, since iteration 1 showed oscillation rising on the s-bend.

After the race: if the oval shows off-track exits or steering_oscillation rises well above 0.37, return to kp 3.5 with kd 0.8 instead of increasing kp further, because kp 3.5 with kd 0.6 gave the best score (556.7) so far.

After the race: if the slalom still ends off track with max_error above 0.06 and line_loss_events near 1.0, test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' only if the last valid signal shows a consistent one-sided exit, and keep ki at 0 unless a one-sided offset appears.
